findings.title: Adding abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is a public provider-factory SPI. Adding `String getShortcut()` with no default means every existing third-party or custom grant type factory fails to compile until it implements the new method, and previously compiled factories can fail at runtime with an abstract-method error when loaded. Since this is an extension point, this is a breaking API change. Provide a default implementation, or make the shortcut optional via a separate interface.

findings.title: Public Context copy constructor removed
findings.body: The public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor has been removed from the public nested class `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. Existing custom grant implementations that clone the context using this constructor will no longer compile, or will fail with `NoSuchMethodError` if already compiled. If removing it is intentional, it should at least be called out as a breaking change because this class is part of the OAuth2 grant provider contract.

findings.title: Default encoder assumes all context shortcuts are exactly 2 characters
findings.body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` hard-codes the encoded prefix length to 6 and splits it into three 2-character shortcuts. However `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` does not enforce a 2-character shortcut and its Javadoc says shortcuts are usually 3 letters. A valid custom grant type with a 3-letter shortcut will be encoded into a 7-character prefix and then later rejected during decoding with `IllegalArgumentException: Expected length of 6`. Shortcut length must be validated and enforced when factories are registered, or the parser must be made resilient to registered non-2-character shortcuts.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check checks grantType twice
findings.body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` where it should validate `rawTokenId`. As a result, a null `rawTokenId` is accepted and stored. Later, `encodeTokenId` can produce a token ID ending with `:null`, and multiple tokens built from null raw IDs could collide. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher logic is inverted
findings.body: The matcher does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, so it rejects exactly the token IDs it is supposed to accept: for an expected authorization-code token, actual ID `onrtac:<uuid>` will return false. It also allows IDs with a different shortcut to pass as long as the UUID part matches. The condition should return `true` on the expected shortcut match, and avoid falling through for a mismatched shortcut.

findings.title: Lazy grant shortcut cache update can create inconsistent reverse mappings
findings.body: In `getShortcutByGrantType`, when a grant type is not cached, the factory is looked up and the shortcut is inserted into both `grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts` without the duplicate validation performed in `postInit`. If a newly deployed grant factory uses a shortcut already mapped to another grant type, `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)` overwrites the old mapping while `grantsToShortcuts` now has two grant types pointing to the same shortcut. The same encoded shortcut will then decode to the new grant even for tokens issued for the older grant, silently corrupting the grant-type context. The lazy refresh path should validate shortcut uniqueness or update the maps consistently.
